note: General home-garden guidance written for LeafScan. 'conditions' are shared cards (keyed by labels.json condition_id); 'classes' override fields for one class; 'plant_care' adds plant-specific care sources to Healthy results. Always check local extension advice and product labels.

healthy.summary: No signs of the problems LeafScan knows for this plant. Keep up good care and re-check regularly, including the undersides of leaves.
actions: Water steadily at the base of the plant
Check leaves weekly - problems are easier to manage early
Re-scan if spots, yellowing, curling or powdery patches appear
prevention: Give plants enough space and light
Keep the area free of weeds and plant debris

sources.title: Home and Landscape pest and disease guides

early_blight.summary: Early blight is a fungal disease (Alternaria) that starts on older, lower leaves and moves upward. Warm, humid weather and soil splash help it spread; it weakens plants gradually.
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric 'target' rings on older leaves
Yellowing around the spots; affected leaves die and drop
Dark lesions on stems
actions: Remove badly affected leaves and bag them; do not compost them
Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves
Water at the base of the plant, early in the day, so leaves dry quickly
If you use a fungicide or pesticide, choose one labelled for this problem and plant, and follow the label
prevention: Rotate tomatoes, potatoes, peppers and eggplant to a new bed for 2-3 years
Clear fallen leaves and plant debris at the end of the season

late_blight.summary: Late blight (Phytophthora infestans) spreads very fast in cool, wet or humid weather and can kill plants within days. It spreads between tomatoes and potatoes, so act quickly.
symptoms: Large pale-green to dark-brown water-soaked patches
White fuzzy growth on leaf undersides when humid
Dark lesions on stems
actions: Remove and bag infected plants or parts; do not compost them
Check nearby tomatoes and potatoes daily
Avoid wetting the foliage
Ask your local extension service or plant clinic to confirm before taking drastic action
prevention: Use healthy transplants and certified seed potatoes
Choose resistant varieties where available

bacterial_spot.summary: Bacterial spot (Xanthomonas and related bacteria) spreads in warm, wet weather through splashing water, wet handling and infected seed or transplants. Infected leaves cannot be cured; the aim is to slow the spread.
symptoms: Small dark, water-soaked spots that turn brown, often with a yellow halo
Spots can merge; leaves yellow and drop
actions: Remove badly affected leaves and bag them; do not compost them
Do not work among plants while they are wet
Water at the base of the plant, early in the day, so leaves dry quickly
Disinfect pruners and tools after working on affected plants
Copper-based sprays may slow spread if started early; follow the label
prevention: Start with disease-free seed and transplants
Rotate crops for 2-3 years
Clear fallen leaves and plant debris at the end of the season

leaf_mold.summary: Tomato leaf mould is a fungal disease of humid, poorly ventilated conditions, especially greenhouses and dense plantings.
symptoms: Pale-yellow patches on the upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety mould underneath
actions: Improve ventilation and lower humidity
Remove badly affected leaves and bag them; do not compost them
Water at the base of the plant, early in the day, so leaves dry quickly
prevention: Space and prune plants so air moves freely around the leaves
Choose resistant varieties

septoria_leaf_spot.summary: Septoria leaf spot is a fungal disease that causes many small spots, starting on lower leaves, and can strip plants of foliage in wet weather.
symptoms: Many small round spots with dark borders and light grey centres
Tiny dark dots in the spot centres
Lower leaves yellow and drop
actions: Remove badly affected leaves and bag them; do not compost them
Mulch to reduce soil splash
Water at the base of the plant, early in the day, so leaves dry quickly
If you use a fungicide or pesticide, choose one labelled for this problem and plant, and follow the label
prevention: Rotate crops
Clear fallen leaves and plant debris at the end of the season
Space and prune plants so air moves freely around the leaves

spider_mites.summary: Spider mites are tiny sap-feeding pests that thrive in hot, dry, dusty conditions. Heavy infestations bronze and dry out leaves.
symptoms: Fine pale speckling (stippling) on leaves
Fine webbing, especially on leaf undersides
Leaves turning bronze or yellow and drying
actions: Hose leaves (especially undersides) to knock mites off
Remove the worst affected leaves
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill the mites' natural enemies
prevention: Keep plants well watered; drought-stressed plants suffer most
Reduce dust around plants

target_spot.summary: Target spot is a fungal leaf disease favoured by warm, wet weather and dense canopies.
symptoms: Brown spots with faint concentric rings, often with a yellow edge
Spots can merge and leaves die
actions: Remove badly affected leaves and bag them; do not compost them
Water at the base of the plant, early in the day, so leaves dry quickly
Space and prune plants so air moves freely around the leaves
If you use a fungicide or pesticide, choose one labelled for this problem and plant, and follow the label
prevention: Rotate crops
Clear fallen leaves and plant debris at the end of the season

leaf_curl_virus.summary: Leaf curl viruses (for example tomato yellow leaf curl and other begomoviruses) are spread by whiteflies. Infected plants cannot be cured.
symptoms: Upward curling, crinkled or cupped leaves
Yellowing leaf edges, stunted growth
Poor flowering and fruit set
actions: Remove and bag infected plants to protect healthy ones
Control whiteflies (sticky traps, insect netting)
Ask your local extension service or plant clinic to confirm before taking drastic action
prevention: Use virus-free transplants and resistant varieties
Keep weeds that host whiteflies under control

mosaic_virus.summary: Mosaic viruses are spread by insects (often aphids), by handling, or in seed and tubers. There is no cure for an infected plant.
symptoms: Light and dark green mottling (mosaic) on leaves
Distorted, puckered or narrow leaves
Stunted growth
actions: Remove and bag infected plants
Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants
Control aphids
prevention: Use virus-free seed, transplants or seed tubers
Choose resistant varieties
Keep weeds that host viruses away

powdery_mildew.summary: Powdery mildews are fungal diseases that grow on the leaf surface. Unlike most leaf diseases they do not need wet leaves, and thrive in shade and warm days with cool nights.
symptoms: White to grey powdery patches on leaves, often starting on the upper surface
Leaves yellow, curl or dry
actions: Remove badly affected leaves
Space and prune plants so air moves freely around the leaves
Keep plants watered at the roots - stressed plants suffer more
If you use a fungicide or pesticide, choose one labelled for this problem and plant, and follow the label
prevention: Choose resistant varieties
Avoid excess nitrogen fertiliser
Grow in full sun

rust.summary: Rusts are fungal diseases that produce masses of powdery spores, usually spread by wind. Many need moist leaves to infect.
symptoms: Orange, rust-brown or yellow pustules, often on the leaf underside
Yellow spots on the upper surface
Leaves yellow and drop
actions: Remove badly affected leaves
Space and prune plants so air moves freely around the leaves
Avoid wetting the foliage
If you use a fungicide or pesticide, choose one labelled for this problem and plant, and follow the label
prevention: Choose resistant varieties
Clear fallen leaves and plant debris at the end of the season

apple_scab.summary: Apple scab is a fungal disease spread by spring rain. It rarely kills trees but spots leaves and fruit and causes early leaf drop.
symptoms: Olive-green to dark velvety spots on leaves
Leaves yellow and fall early
Dark scabby spots on fruit
actions: Rake up and remove fallen leaves in autumn
Prune to open the canopy
If you use a fungicide or pesticide, choose one labelled for this problem and plant, and follow the label
prevention: Choose scab-resistant varieties
Clear fallen leaves and plant debris at the end of the season

black_rot.summary: Black rot is a fungal disease that overwinters on mummified fruit and infected wood, and spreads in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Brown leaf spots, often with a darker border or ring
Tiny black dots (fruiting bodies) in the spots
Shrivelled black fruit (mummies)
actions: Remove mummified fruit and dead wood
Remove badly affected leaves and bag them; do not compost them
If you use a fungicide or pesticide, choose one labelled for this problem and plant, and follow the label
prevention: Space and prune plants so air moves freely around the leaves
Clear fallen leaves and plant debris at the end of the season

citrus_greening.summary: Citrus greening (Huanglongbing, HLB) is a bacterial disease spread by the Asian citrus psyllid. It is incurable and eventually kills trees; in many regions it must be reported.
symptoms: Blotchy, asymmetrical yellow mottling of leaves
Yellow shoots, small upright leaves
Small, lopsided, bitter fruit
actions: Contact your local agriculture or extension service - HLB is a regulated disease in many places
Look for psyllids on new growth
prevention: Buy citrus only from certified nurseries
Do not move citrus plants or cuttings between areas

gray_leaf_spot.summary: Gray leaf spot of corn is a fungal disease favoured by warm, humid weather and corn residue left on the soil.
symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular grey to tan lesions between leaf veins
Lesions merge and leaves die
actions: Remove badly affected leaves in small plantings
Space and prune plants so air moves freely around the leaves
prevention: Rotate corn with other crops
Bury or remove crop residue
Choose resistant varieties

leaf_blight.summary: Leaf blights are fungal diseases that cause large dead areas on leaves, favoured by warm, wet weather and long leaf wetness.
symptoms: Large tan, brown or grey lesions
Lesions merge; leaves die back
actions: Remove badly affected leaves and bag them; do not compost them
Water at the base of the plant, early in the day, so leaves dry quickly
Space and prune plants so air moves freely around the leaves
If you use a fungicide or pesticide, choose one labelled for this problem and plant, and follow the label
prevention: Rotate crops
Clear fallen leaves and plant debris at the end of the season
Choose resistant varieties

sources.title: Home and Landscape pest and disease guides

esca.summary: Esca (black measles) is a fungal trunk disease of grapevines spread through pruning wounds. Infected vines decline over years.
symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' yellow or red patches between leaf veins that dry out
Dark spots on berries
actions: Mark affected vines and prune them last
Disinfect pruners and tools after working on affected plants
Ask your local extension service or plant clinic to confirm before taking drastic action
prevention: Prune in dry weather
Protect large pruning wounds

leaf_scorch.summary: Strawberry leaf scorch is a fungal disease that causes many small purple spots and can weaken plants.
symptoms: Many small dark-purple spots on the upper leaf surface
Spots merge; leaves look scorched and dry
actions: Remove badly affected leaves and bag them; do not compost them
Water at the base of the plant, early in the day, so leaves dry quickly
prevention: Replace old plantings every few years
Use healthy runners
Space and prune plants so air moves freely around the leaves

actions: Remove and bag infected foliage or plants; do not compost them
If foliage is badly affected, remove it and wait before harvesting so tubers are less likely to be infected
Store only sound tubers
Ask your local extension service or plant clinic to confirm before taking drastic action

peach_bacterial_spot.summary: Bacterial spot of peach (Xanthomonas arboricola) spreads in warm, wet, windy weather and causes leaf spots, early leaf drop and fruit spots.

sources.title: Home and Landscape pest and disease guides

apple_cedar_apple_rust.summary: Cedar apple rust is a fungal disease that alternates between apple and juniper (cedar) trees; spores blow from galls on junipers in wet spring weather.
symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface
Small tube-like structures under the spots later in summer

corn_northern_leaf_blight.summary: Northern leaf blight of corn is a fungal disease that causes long cigar-shaped lesions and is favoured by moderate temperatures and heavy dew.
